verdict.rationale: LaunchDarkly documents separate environments spanning local development through production, and users can create as many as they need. An AI client can manage environments through the CLI and MCP server, so testing can run in a non-production environment rather than as a mere dry run. However, the evidence never explicitly states that non-production environments are isolated from production data, nor does it describe a dedicated sandbox mode. Missing for 10: explicit documentation that environments isolate production flag/context data, a documented sandbox or test-environment workflow for agents (e.g., environment-scoped MCP/API access), and hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data

citations.quote: Environments allow you to manage your feature flags throughout your entire development lifecycle, from local development through production.
You can create as many additional environments as you need.
set up and manage your feature flags, account members, projects, environments, teams, and other resources directly from the command line.
